method: Scope was assigned only where a university repository, publisher description, publisher-hosted abstract or publisher issue record described the work in enough detail to distinguish an edition, synthesis, thematic study or provenance-and-ethics study. Titles alone were not treated as sufficient evidence.
policy: These notes support work-level scope classification only. They make no claim about complete object extraction, preferred readings, object identity, authenticity, rights, or permission to reproduce text or images.

entries.finding: The HSE University record says the State Hermitage holds eleven bowls and that the paper is the first publication of the entire collection, based on collations of the originals.

Wayne State University Press describes a comprehensive study of early Jewish magic covering the phenomenon, sources, research methods and history of scholarship, with bowls among a wider body of evidence.

entries.locator: https://traffickingculture.org/app/uploads/2014/11/Brodie-2014-Incantation-Bowls.pdf; published version represented by the indexed 2016 chapter
entries.finding: The complete article hosted by the University of Glasgow-led Trafficking Culture project states in its abstract and conclusion that it examines legal and ethical problems raised by collecting and studying unprovenanced, likely looted incantation bowls.
The journal abstract identifies the contribution as a response to arguments about Morgenstern's edition of BM 135563 and its terminology, rather than a new edition or a bounded object corpus.

The chapter preview explicitly calls the work a preliminary survey of the Moussaieff Collection's Mandaic-script magic texts; it notes that only selected Jewish-script items had been published and that other materials were being prepared elsewhere.
The journal record places Stadel's four-page discussion of Aramaic Bowl Spells volume one in the issue's Reviews section; it is a scholarly review, not the reviewed corpus edition itself.

Brill places Lusini's two-page contribution in the issue's Recensioni section, and the publisher-hosted text reviews Moriggi's methods, corpus coverage and linguistic contribution rather than presenting a separate object edition.

deferred.reason: The university record provides a licensed full-text link but no abstract, while the publisher page exposes no abstract without paid access. The work remains unclassified rather than relying on its title alone.
Project MUSE blocks automated inspection and the accessible authoritative issue record gives only the title and pages. A third-party abstract was not used as the classification basis.

The official article identifies Mykhailo Yelnykov as author and concerns a fourteenth-century Arabic metal magic bowl rather than a late-antique Aramaic incantation bowl. The indexed authorship and collection relevance need bibliographic review before any scope decision.
